title: [Bugfix] glm47 parser: tolerate missing opening <arg_value> tag
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

FIX #49248

Under concurrent load, GLM-4.7-family models sporadically skip the opening `<arg_value>` tag when emitting tool calls, producing

```
<tool_call>search<arg_key>query</arg_key>how many vacation days left</arg_value></tool_call>
```

with the argument value fully intact (raw sampled tokens captured via `logprobs: true`; reproduces at `temperature: 0` too, ~5–17% of calls at concurrency 6 on our production trace family, 0 sequentially).

`_ARG_RE`/`_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` in `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py` require the opening tag, so such calls silently parse to `arguments: "{}"`, which then fails the client's tool schema validation and degrades agent loops (the broken `{}` call gets rendered back into history, so retries tend to fail the same way).

This PR makes the opening `<arg_value>` optional in both regexes. The closing `</arg_value>` still delimits the value, so:
- well-formed output parses exactly as before (the optional group matches the tag when present);
- streaming is unaffected: the incremental lexer buffers ambiguous tag prefixes, so a partially streamed `<arg_value>` never leaks into a value snapshot.

## Test Plan

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py`: new non-streaming cases (single arg with missing opening tag; mixed malformed + well-formed args in one call) and a streaming case with the malformed sequence split across chunks; all pre-existing cases unchanged.
- Live validation on a 4×GPU GLM-5.2 deployment (`--tool-call-parser glm47`), replaying the production request that triggers the malformation at concurrency 6 with `logprobs: true`:
  - before: 12/120 responses parsed to `arguments: "{}"`;
  - after: 12/72 responses still show the raw malformation in sampled tokens (model-side quirk, expected), **all 12 parse to full arguments**, 0 empty; streaming replay 0/72 empty.

## Test Result

`pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py` — 16 passed.

title: [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training
bodyExcerpt:
# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))
2. **Adapter-only sync missing**: frameworks must merge LoRA → send full weights → unmerge. Adapter-only sync (send only LoRA delta, load via vLLM's LoRA serving) would eliminate the merge round-trip ([trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975))
3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO
- [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776): LoRA + MoE inference mismatch investigation
- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes
- Adapter-only sync path available (no full-weight merge required)

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

title: Update vendored LMCache connector for current IPCCacheServerKey API
bodyExcerpt:
## What

The vendored fallback LMCache connector (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_integration/multi_process_adapter.py`) was stale relative to the current `lmcache` package API:

1. **`IPCCacheEngineKey` → `IPCCacheServerKey`**: The key class was renamed in the LMCache codebase. The vendored connector still imported the old name, which would cause `ImportError` if the fallback path were ever reached.

2. **`tp_size` field → `use_mla` field**: `IPCCacheServerKey` no longer has a `tp_size` constructor argument. It now has `use_mla: bool` (backward-compatible msgspec field, defaults `False`). Both `_create_key` methods updated to pass `use_mla=self.parallel_strategy.use_mla`.

3. **`chunk_hash` field removed**: `IPCCacheServerKey` no longer supports hash-mode keys (the `chunk_hash` field was removed). The `_create_hash_key` methods now raise `NotImplementedError` with a clear message directing users to the token-based `_create_key` path or to install the `lmcache` package (which has the current, fully-maintained adapter).

## Why

This vendored connector is a **fallback** — it is only used when `from lmcache.integration.vllm.vllm_multi_process_adapter import ...` fails (i.e., the `lmcache` package is not installed). In the normal case (lmcache installed), the LMCache-tree adapter is used instead, which is kept in sync with the API.

However, if the fallback is ever reached (e.g., partial install, version mismatch), the stale imports would cause confusing `ImportError`/`TypeError` crashes. This PR makes the fallback at least importable and gives clear error messages for the removed hash-mode API.

title: [Bugfix] Pick a KV block size supported by every attention backend
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #48286.

`Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` picks the KV cache block size from the **first** non-SSM attention backend only. Models that mix attention backends with disjoint block-size support break: GLM-DSA / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models pair a sparse-MLA main backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, supports `[32, 64]`, prefers 32) with `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (supports only `[64]`). The auto-selected 32 then fails much later in `select_common_block_size()` with the opaque

```
ValueError: No common block size for 32.
```

and the only workaround is a manual `--block-size 64` (undocumented, as #48286 notes).

This PR was split in two to keep the diff reviewable. It now carries backend collection and block-size selection only (+131/-21). Aligning phases 2 and 3 to the full backend list follows in a separate PR once this one merges.

## Changes

- `Platform._find_non_ssm_backend()` becomes `_find_non_ssm_backends()` and returns every distinct non-SSM backend in layer order rather than the first. Both call sites are updated (`interface.py`, `cpu.py`); no caller of the old name remains.
- New `Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends()` returns the smallest block size every backend accepts:
  - a single backend keeps today's behaviour via `get_preferred_block_size()`;
  - if every backend accepts the default, the default wins;
  - otherwise candidates are the least common multiples formed by taking one supported size per backend, tried in ascending order, and **each candidate is confirmed against every backend** via `supports_block_size()`;
  - if nothing is common it raises `ValueError` naming each backend and its supported sizes.
- Candidates are validated rather than inferred. A backend may override `supports_block_size()` to accept exact sizes only, as CPU_MLA does by accepting 16 but no multiple of it, so "a multiple of a supported size" is not a safe assumption. This is the correctness point @yewentao256 raised in review.

title: [Bugfix] Fix SM100 fp8_ds_mla cache scales
bodyExcerpt:
# Fix the SM100 fp8_ds_mla cache scale mismatch

## Summary

This change rounds each `fp8_ds_mla` tile scale up to an E8M0-compatible
power of two on SM100 and later GPUs.

The change applies to both cache writers:

- the native CUDA writer;
- the fused DeepSeek-V3.2 Triton writer.

## Problem

Each writer used an arbitrary 32-bit floating-point (FP32) scale to quantize
an E4M3 tile. The writer then stored this FP32 scale in the cache.

On SM100, FlashMLA converts the stored scale to E8M0 before dequantization.
Thus, FlashMLA used a different scale from the writer. This mismatch increased
the dequantization error.

The change rounds the scale up before quantization. The writer and FlashMLA
now use the same scale. Rounding down could make the largest tile value
overflow E4M3.

GPUs before SM100 keep the existing behavior.

I ran these targeted tests on one NVIDIA B300 GPU:

title: [rocm] perf: drop redundant -inf prefill of decode paged MQA-logits buffer
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Removes the full-width `out_logits.fill_(float("-inf"))` before the decode paged MQA-logits kernel in `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`).

The decode consumer, `top_k_per_row_decode`, bounds its per-row scan by `seq_lens` (it reads only `[0, rowEnd)` where `rowEnd = seq_len - next_n + next_n_idx + 1`) and pads short rows (`rowLen <= topK`) with `-1` internally. The paged MQA-logits kernels write every in-causal column that top-k reads:
- Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` writes `-inf` into masked in-tile positions itself.
- FlyDSL `flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` writes exactly `col <= q_limit` (== the columns top-k reads).

So the out-of-window `[rowEnd, max_model_len)` region initialized by this `fill_` is never consumed on the decode path, making the prefill redundant. Dropping it saves a `rows x max_model_len` fp32 HBM write every decode step.

## Why it's safe (decode path)

`q_limit` (kernel write extent) and `rowEnd` (top-k read extent) are both derived from the same context length and `next_n`, so every column top-k reads is freshly written; nothing reads the untouched tail.

## Scope / caveats

- Only affects the **decode** paged path (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`).
- The prefill top-k path and the `topk_indices_buffer[...] = -1` init are untouched.
- The FlyDSL kernel documents a `-inf`-prefill contract; this change relies on the consumer's `seq_lens` bounding rather than the kernel self-initializing, so it should be validated numerically.

## Test plan

- [ ] Compare decode top-k indices with/without the fill across short / long / padded batches (Gluon and FlyDSL paths) on gfx942/gfx950.
- [ ] Run existing `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` and sparse-indexer tests.
- [ ] Sanity-check end-to-end GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA decode output.

bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a bug where any `/v1/chat/completions` request with tools whose JSON Schema
contains `$defs`/`definitions` fails with HTTP 500 on Cohere models served with
`--reasoning-parser cohere_command3|cohere_command4`.

Resolves the bug class reported in #16467 (closed as stale, never fixed) for the
Cohere reasoning parser path specifically. Other parsers that compose their own
grammars are out of scope (see the GLM case in #47175); the generic tool path in
`vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` already hoists `$defs` and is unaffected.

**Root cause.** `collect_tool_schema` in
`vllm/reasoning/cohere_command_reasoning_parser.py` builds the constrained-decoding
grammar for tool calls by nesting each tool's `parameters` schema inside a
`{tool_call_id, tool_name, parameters}` envelope. The tool schema was spliced in
verbatim, so a definitions block originally at the schema root ends up under
`properties.parameters`, while its `$ref` pointers (`#/$defs/X`) remain
root-anchored. xgrammar then correctly rejects the dangling JSON pointer:

```text
RuntimeError: Cannot find field $defs in #/$defs/X
```

The request fails during preprocessing, before generation. Agentic frameworks such as pydantic-ai emit `$defs`
for any nested model, so this breaks effectively all tools defined via such
frameworks (see user reports in #16467).

`--reasoning-parser cohere_command4 --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 --enable-auto-tool-choice`

title: [Core][PCP][Output] Restore only sampled final rows after PCP prefill
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

PCP currently gathers and reorders every scheduled hidden-state row after the final layer, although ordinary sampling needs only the final row of each request. This PR exchanges only those sampled rows and passes them directly to logits computation.

```text
ASIS
rank-local hidden states
  -> AllGather all scheduled rows
  -> restore global token order
  -> select final rows
  -> logits and sampling
```

```text
PR
rank-local hidden states
  -> pack owned final rows
  -> multicast compact rows and synchronize
  -> restore request order
  -> logits and sampling
```

Pure decode uses the already-replicated rows without communication. Active prompt logprobs and TP-sharded sampling retain dense restoration. Systems without multicast use compact collective exchange; the one-row prefill case retains the existing collective.

## Implementation

- Compute sampled-row ownership while constructing the PCP layout.
- Reuse pinned metadata buffers and double-buffered sampled outputs.
- Construct the dense inverse map only when needed.
- Preserve resumed multi-row decode indexing and current graph-padding behavior.
- Allocate multicast storage before KV-cache profiling and release it on shutdown.
- Use PyTorch `multimem_all_gather_out`, which combines multicast stores and cross-rank synchronization in one CUDA kernel.

This changes transient final hidden-state restoration. It does not change KV-cache placement or quantization and is independent of #52863's direct KV-update publication.

## Controlled full-model engine results

The comparison used the full GLM-5.2 NVFP4 checkpoint on 4x GB200:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Parallelism | TP1 / PCP4 / EP4 / DCP1 |
| Execution | Eager, Torch 2.13 |
| Attention | FLASH_ATTN MLA prefill; FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE decode |
| MoE / KV format | flashinfer_cutlass / FP8 |
| Workload | 4 requests, each with 1024 input and 32 greedy output tokens |
| Cache / scheduling | Prefix caching off; chunked prefill on; 1024 cache blocks |

title: [Perf][Kernel] Fused DSA indexer Top-k kernel (LiteTopk)
bodyExcerpt:
## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Keep unquantized routed experts unquantized under AutoGPTQ
bodyExcerpt:
# Issue #49141 — Fused_moe dimension mismatch for Qwen MXFP4 model on ROCm

## 1. Root cause

The issue has two reports. Both are the same underlying defect: **a MoE layer whose
expert weights are stored *unquantized* in the checkpoint is still given a
*quantized* MoE method**, so the allocated parameters do not match the checkpoint
tensors.

The trigger in both cases is the MTP (speculative-decoding drafter) layer. AMD's
Quark and community GPTQ quantizations of `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` quantize the 40
transformer layers but leave the MTP layer's experts in bf16. The main model
loads fine; only the drafter fails.

* **Original MXFP4/Quark report** (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must
  match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1`, in
  `routed_experts.py::_load_w2`).
  `hidden_size=2048`, `moe_intermediate_size=512`. Quark MXFP4 allocates
  `w2_weight` as `(E, hidden, intermediate // 2)` = `(E, 2048, 256)` (fp4 packs
  two values per byte), while the checkpoint's MTP `down_proj.weight` is the
  unquantized `(2048, 512)`. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`'s
  `quantization_config.exclude` lists `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.<i>.{gate,up,down}_proj`
  for all 256 experts, but `should_ignore_layer()` only compared the *parent*
  layer name `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts` against those *child* entries.
  **This half is already fixed on main** by the `check_children` argument added
  to `quark/utils.py::should_ignore_layer` (the amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 fix), which is
  why a commenter on the issue could not reproduce it on main. No change needed.

* **Still-broken GPTQ report** (issue comments:
  `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_weight'. Did you
  mean: 'w2_qweight'?`, same drafter-loading path).
  `AutoGPTQConfig` tracks which modules the checkpoint actually quantized in
  `modules_in_block_to_quantize` — auto-derived in `maybe_update_config()` from
  the safetensors dtypes, so it contains only the quantized layers' per-expert
  module name

title: [Bug] Modular MoE reports zero local experts after a backend releases source weights
bodyExcerpt:
## Bug

A modular MoE backend that prepares its own expert-weight owner and then releases the source weights fails during startup profiling because `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl` derives `local_num_experts` from `w1.shape[0]`.

The downstream B12X EP integration reproduces this with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP8/DCP4/EP8 on 8x RTX PRO 6000:

```text
ValueError: B12X EP local expert metadata does not match prepared weights: metadata=0, prepared=32
```

Failing run + logs: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/30186408654/job/89751956320

## Cause

B12X intentionally replaces the source `w13`/`w2` parameters with empty tensors after preparing its packed expert owner. The generic modular wrapper subsequently reports zero local experts, while the backend-owned prepared weights still contain the correct 32.

The backend's `moe_problem_size()` can recover the prepared expert count, but the modular path does not use that value for workspace metadata.

## Expected

Released source weights should not erase backend-owned expert metadata, and real expert-count mismatches should continue to fail.

Fixes #49649.

FlashInfer's sparse-MLA attention kernels (`sparse_mla_sm120`) livelock GB10 (sm_121) GPUs under cold-prefill load, wedging entire TP clusters with no host-side recovery path. # [Bug][DCP] DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 fused attention bypasses pure-DCP handling

## Problem

The fused DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 path still has two pure-DCP correctness
defects:

1. `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/common/kernels.py` checks owner-local KV slot
   validity before query RMSNorm. A negative slot means another DCP rank owns
   the token's KV entry; it does not remove this rank's query contribution.
2. `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py` gathers query heads and combines
   partial output/LSE only for PCP+DCP. Pure DCP therefore sends rank-local
   query heads into attention over owner-local KV and never performs the
   required cross-rank result merge.

The sparse-indexer DCP rank, world-size, and interleave plumbing mentioned in
the original report has landed independently on `main`; it is no longer part
of this issue.

## Observable regression

A focused kernel reproducer uses an all-negative slot mapping, representing a
DCP rank that owns no KV-cache slot for those tokens.

Expected:

- Query output matches reference RMSNorm.
- MLA and indexer KV caches remain unchanged.
- The Top-K buffer is cleared.

Actual on unpatched `main`:

- Query output remains zero because the kernel returns before query RMSNorm.

At model level, @drakosha reproduced repeated-token output on unpatched
GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with TP4/DCP4 and `fp8_ds_mla`. The patched path produced output
byte-identical to DCP1 for the tested deterministic greedy request.

## Expected behavior

- Query RMSNorm runs independently of owner-local KV-slot validity.
- Negative slots continue to suppress MLA and indexer KV-cache writes.
- Pure DCP gathers query heads before owner-local sparse attention.
- Partial output/LSE is combined across DCP ranks through the existing DCP
  manager.

## Proposed fix and validation

PR #50005 implements the fix and regression coverage.

At its current head:

- The focused fused norm/RoPE suite passes all 67 tests on GB200.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks pass.

title: Malformed /v1/responses request returns a >100MB validation-error body (full input echoed per error)
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

A single malformed `POST /v1/responses` request can produce an **HTTP 400 response body over 100 MB**, because the request's entire `input` payload is echoed **once per validation error**. With an input that produces thousands of validation errors, the response size explodes far beyond the request size — a response-amplification / DoS vector against clients and any proxy in front of vLLM.

### Environment

- vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev601+ga16dbd5b8` (nightly), OpenAI-compatible server, Responses API (`/v1/responses`).
- Served model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (FP8), text-only. (The model is incidental — this is server-side request validation, not model behavior.)

### What happens

When an `/v1/responses` request has an `input` whose shape fails Pydantic validation (e.g. `input` given as a list of message-shaped objects where a field has the wrong type), the server returns a 400 whose body is a Pydantic validation-error dump. Each individual error entry **embeds the full offending `input` value** under its `input` key. For a request with N content items that each fail, you get ~N error entries, each carrying a copy of the whole payload.

Observed in production: one such request produced **12,047 validation errors** and a **~114 MB response body** from a request of a few KB. Representative (truncated) error entry:

```

```

- Clients and proxies must buffer/parse a 100 MB+ body for what should be a small 400.
- In our case the downstream proxy (LiteLLM) read and post-processed the entire body, stalling its event loop and inflating memory — a small malformed request cascaded into a service outage. (Filing the proxy-side hardening separately with that project.)

### Motivation

GLM-5.x models can spend the whole completion budget in the reasoning phase when thinking is enabled by default. This makes OpenAI-compatible chat/tool-calling flows difficult to use unless the caller explicitly disables thinking or sets a small `thinking_token_budget`.

In a local vLLM 0.24.0 deployment, `thinking_token_budget` already works with GLM-5.2 when serving with:

```bash

  --enable-auto-tool-choice \

- #20859 added the hard thinking-token limit.

For engine-based parsers, streaming and non-streaming produce **different `content`** for the same model output when plain text sits immediately before, between, or after a tool call.

The non-streaming path strips whitespace from tool-associated content (`_strip_content_whitespace` → `content.strip()` in `vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`, gated by config flag `strip_content_whitespace_with_tools`, default `True`). ## Summary

`thinking_token_budget` (added in #20859) hard-rejects on the V2 model runner with:

```
thinking_token_budget is not yet supported by the V2 model runner.
Run vLLM with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 to use thinking_token_budget.
```

Request: port the thinking-budget logits processor (force-close the reasoning phase after N reasoning tokens, via the registered reasoning parser) to the V2 model runner.

## Motivation

We serve Moonshot Kimi-K3 (hybrid KDA/linear-attention arch — `IsHybrid` + `HasInnerState`, separate mamba-cache state) on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3` image, which defaults to V2. The model's default reasoning effort (`thinking_effort=max` when the client omits it) can spend the entire output budget inside the reasoning phase, producing `finish_reason=length` responses with reasoning-only output and zero client-visible content. On our production gateway this terminal class ("reasoning_only empty output") occurs at ~27 per 10K requests on K3 vs ~1.3 per 10K on comparable thinking models.

`thinking_token_budget` is exactly the right governor and works for our non-V2 models (Kimi K2.6, GLM-5.1/5.2) — it force-closes reasoning so content always gets budget. It is unavailable precisely on the one model in our fleet that most needs it.

The V1-runner workaround (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) is likely a non-starter for hybrid/mamba architectures like K3, so a V1 fallback is not a real remediation path here.

## Proposed scope

Support `thinking_token_budget` (chat + completions protocols) under the V2 runner for models with a registered `--reasoning-parser`, with the same semantics as the V1 implementation: inject the reasoning-end token when the budget is reached, preserving the remaining max_tokens budget for content.

title: [Bugfix][Model] Remove redundant all_gather_interleave in ViT split_qkv
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #49061.

PaddleOCR-VL, Ernie4.5-VL, and GLM-4.1V vision attention each carried a
byte-identical helper `all_gather_interleave()` that calls
`torch.distributed.all_gather()` directly on the tensor-parallel group's raw
`device_group`, followed by a per-rank re-split, inside `split_qkv()`.

There are two problems.

First, portability. The vision encoder runs eagerly (`torch.no_grad()`, outside
`torch.compile`). On any platform whose `device_group` has no c10d backend
registered for eager use, the direct `dist.all_gather()` raises
`RuntimeError: No backend type associated with device type`, which crashes the
vision-encoder worker with `EngineDeadError` for every image request at
`tensor_parallel_size > 1`. vLLM's collective API
(`tensor_model_parallel_all_gather`, routed through `GroupCoordinator`) exists to
handle exactly this case, and the hand-rolled helper bypassed it.

Second, redundancy. The gather is a no-op. Each rank's local qkv out of
`QKVParallelLinear` (`gather_output=False`) is `[q_shard | k_shard | v_shard]`
for that rank's own heads. `all_gather_interleave` gathers every rank, reorders
to `[all_q | all_k | all_v]`, then `split_tensor_along_last_dim(...)[tp_rank]`
selects back exactly this rank's own shards. For full multi-head self-attention
(`total_num_kv_heads == total_num_heads`, which all three models use) the whole
round-trip is a numerical identity, so chunking the local tensor directly is
bit-identical.

This is the same removal already merged for `glm4_1v` in #23441
("Remove redundant all gather + split"), which fixed that model's `split_qkv`
but left the now-dead `all_gather_interleave` helper behind.

## Changes

- `paddleocr_vl.py`, `ernie45_vl.py`: drop the `all_gather_interleave` gather and
  the subsequent per-rank re-split from `split_qkv`, keeping `qkv.chunk(3, dim=2)`
  and the reshape. This matches the already-merged `glm4_1v.split_qkv`.
- All three files: delete the now-unused module-level `all_gather_interleave`.

title: Add MoNe experts pruning support
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Mixture of Novices and Experts (MoNe) is an expert pruning method accepted at ICLR-2026 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.00390
 
The method computes statistics (access frequency and output variance) about experts during calibration, identifies redundant experts and replaces them with constant vectors which are their unbiased estimators. MoNe is planned to be supported in the llm-compressor https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2906 

Given MoNe replaces redundant expert's MLP blocks with constant vectors, it requires custom support in vllm. 

This PR is the first self-contained step toward broader MoNE support. It introduces an algorithm-independent expert-substitution checkpoint contract and implements the minimal constant-v1 inference path for unquantized DeepSeek/GLM models using the Triton backend and tensor parallelism. It intentionally does not support additional model families, replacement formats, quantized experts, expert/data parallelism, or other MoE backends.

# [Bugfix][DCP] Fix NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 fused attention

Fixes #50095.

## Purpose

Fix two DCP correctness defects in the fused DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2
attention path:

- The fused norm/RoPE kernel skipped query RMSNorm when a DCP rank had no
  owner-local KV-cache slot. KV ownership does not remove that rank's query
  contribution.
- Pure DCP sent only rank-local query heads into attention over owner-local KV
  and did not combine the resulting partial output/LSE across DCP ranks.

The sparse-indexer DCP rank, world-size, and interleave plumbing described in
the original version of this PR has since landed independently on `main`; this
PR no longer changes that part.

## Implementation

- Run query RMSNorm before the owner-local slot check. Negative slots still
  suppress MLA and indexer KV-cache writes.
- For pure DCP, gather query heads through `MLADCPManager` before sparse MLA
  attention. The manager keeps the direct-workspace fast path when supported
  and falls back safely for oversized mixed batches.
- Combine partial output/LSE through the existing `MLADCPManager` after
  attention. For this NVIDIA pure-DCP mixed-batch path, pass no PCP-only decode
  metadata; its sparse backend supplies neutral contributions for empty local
  shards.
- Extend the existing fused norm/RoPE test with an all-negative-slot regression
  that checks valid query output, unchanged caches, and Top-K clearing.

## Non-duplication

I re-audited related open work on August 23, 2026. Searching for issue #50095
finds only this PR.

- #52472 adds a separate TurboQuant sparse MLA backend and does not modify this

title: [Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark draft support under decode context parallelism
bodyExcerpt:
### What

Make dense (GQA/MHA) DFlash/DSpark drafts work under `decode_context_parallel_size > 1`
by caching the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank.

Rebased on `main` after #52188. That PR landed the DCP-aware draft slot mapping this
branch used to carry (`cp_local_slot` / `prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens` in
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`), and its version is strictly better: it also handles
the null block and the rejected context suffix. That commit is dropped here in favour
of upstream's, leaving the part #52188 does not cover.

#52188 enables the MLA draft path (Kimi-K3, one latent KV head, no head-gather). This
PR enables the dense path, where the head-gather is exactly what breaks.

### Why (root cause)

Reported by @Leoyzen in #46514: DFlash/DSpark acceptance collapses to ~0% under DCP.

The dense flash DCP path (`_forward_with_dcp`: all-gather query heads across the DCP
group, attend against the rank-local KV shard, LSE-merge) is only correct when a rank's
KV shard holds the KV heads for all gathered query heads, i.e. KV heads replicated
across the DCP group. `verify_with_parallel_config` enforces this for dense *targets*;
nothing checked the *draft*. The GLM-5.2 DSpark draft is MHA (64q/64kv), so under TP4
each rank has a 16-head shard and the gathered 64 query heads are GQA-remapped 4:1 onto
the wrong KV heads.

### How

Cache the whole DCP group's KV heads on every rank (replicated) for that rank's
interleaved positions:

- `cache_num_kv_heads` decouples the KV-cache spec from the impl's head count
  (`Attention.__init__`, defaults to `num_kv_heads`, only larger for this case).
- The draft precompute all-gathers K/V across the DCP group in the same rank order the
  query gather uses, so MHA maps 1:1 and GQA stays contiguous.
- The query block's K/V is not slotted into such a cache: the DCP path attends it
  against the freshly computed K/V, and at input-prep time the rank holds only its
  local heads, so writing them would corrupt the replicated layou

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: store draft KV cache in model dtype for MLA-only cache layouts; fail fast on DCP
bodyExcerpt:
FIX #48380

Two DSpark fixes for DSA-family targets:

1. **Draft cache dtype.** With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` the DSpark draft — a dense (non-MLA) Qwen3-style transformer — inherited the target's `cache_config` and tried to use the MLA-only fp8_ds_mla layout, which no dense attention backend accepts (`ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda ...`). `load_dspark_model` now falls back to the model dtype for the draft's KV cache; the draft cache is a few dense layers, so the memory cost is negligible.

title: [Quantization][ModelOpt] Serve modelopt_mixed checkpoints with FP8_PB layers
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Serves `modelopt_mixed` checkpoints containing FP8_PB layers. Rebased onto #49381.

FP8_PB and FP8_PB_WO are the same quantization scheme — per-block FP8 with dynamic
per-token activation quant — resolving to the same QuantKey pair and the same block-FP8
kernel. They differ only in scale serialization: FP8_PB_WO exports ModelOpt's 4-D
`weight_scale` [out_blk, 1, in_blk, 1], which requires every partition to be
block-aligned; FP8_PB uses DeepSeek's 2-D `weight_scale_inv`, sized by ceiling division,
so a partition may end in a partial block.

GLM-5.2 needs the latter. `q_a_proj` (2048) + `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` (576) fuse to a
2624-wide `fused_qkv_a_proj`; `2624 % 128 = 64`, and the layer is replicated, so no TP
degree makes it block-aligned. Previously this failed with
`KeyError: '...weight_scale_inv'`.

## Design

Since the layout can't live in the QuantKey, it rides on `CkptCtx.block_scale_deepseek`
— the per-checkpoint carrier #49381 already provides — and `KFp8Block128` branches on it.
`FormatScheme` is the wrong seam: it composes *around* the key schemes and can't replace
what the weight scheme registers, and a secondpossible for the
same key.

Adding FP8_PB is one `LINEAR_ALGOS` row plus one `resolve()` row. No new sub-config —
`resolve()` only reads `subcfg` for the NVFP4 LinearKernel`
already reads whichever scale name is present, so no kernel change.

`kFp8Static128BlockSym` is 128x128, so a checkpoint declaring another `group_size` is
rejected at config time rather than silently m

## Two fixes to existing behavior

1. `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` never implems()`, which
   `VllmConfig` uses to enable `+quant_fp8`. Without it `QuantFP8` runs `forward_native`,
   emitting unpacked fp32 group scales where Dwants them
   UE8M0-packed into int32 — the model serves NaN logits. Resolving it per layer fixes
   FP8_PB_WO mixed checkpoints too, not just F

2. `deep_gemm_warmup` discovered layers via `ip8LinearMethod)

Reuse VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING as the reviewer-suggested tri-state server override for structural-tag based tool calling:

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Warm spec-sized logits all-gather during init
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes DeepSeek/GLM-5.2 MTP speculative decoding hanging at startup (#48568).

Warmup runs `compute_logits`' vocab-parallel all-gather at one row per request, but spec decode verifies `max_num_reqs*(1+num_speculative_tokens)` rows. On ROCm/RCCL the larger message connects extra channels lazily on first use, so when that first use is a live decode step the connect fails (`no transport for peer on channel N`) and the engine hangs. Warm `compute_logits` at the spec-decode row count during init.

Serve GLM-5.2-FP8 with MTP speculative decoding on 8x MI300X (gfx942):

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
```

## Test Result

Server starts and serves normally with MTP speculative decoding, producing coherent completions. Without this change the engine hangs in the logits all-gather on the first speculative-decode step.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Sync reused pinned input buffers under PP batch queue (fixes IMA with sparse MLA + PP)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix a race on reused pinned CPU input buffers when engine steps overlap under the PP batch queue.

`prepare_inputs_event` (consumed by `synchronize_input_prep()`) was only created when async scheduling is enabled. But the PP batch queue creates exactly the same overlap (`max_concurrent_batches == pp_size`): input prep for step N+1 rewrites the reused pinned CPU tensors (`seq_lens_cpu`, `query_start_loc_cpu`, block-table staging, …) while step N's `non_blocking` H2D copies from those same buffers may not have executed yet. When the copy engine finally runs, step N's kernels consume step N+1's values.

For DSA sparse-MLA models this is fatal rather than silent: the indexer sizes its prefill-chunk buffers from step N's CPU values but its GPU kernels index with the (now newer, possibly larger) device `seq_lens` — out-of-bounds scatter → `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Reported in the field in #38476 (multi-node TP×PP, and single-node repro below). For dense models the same race can silently corrupt inputs.

The fix creates the event whenever `max_concurrent_batches > 1`, so `synchronize_input_prep()` guards every overlapped-step configuration (async scheduling ⇒ ≥ 2; PP ⇒ pp_size). Single-batch configurations are unchanged.

## Why the symptom is so elusive

- `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` makes every H2D copy synchronous → pinned buffers are always consumed before reuse → 100% stable (verified). This masks the bug in exactly the debugging mode people reach for.
- TP-only has `max_concurrent_batches == 1` → unaffected.
- The window is proportional to how far the GPU lags the CPU — huge on SM80 with Triton sparse-MLA prefill (#47629), narrow-but-nonzero on H100.

title: [Bug]: DeepGemm accuracy auto-disable (_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES) does not apply to the FP8 MoE path
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: NVIDIA GB10, **SM121 / compute capability 12.1** (also relevant to SM120 generally)
- vLLM **0.26.0** (standard PyPI wheel, aarch64), torch 2.11.0+cu130, `--enforce-eager`, TP=1
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` — `model_type: **qwen3_5_moe_text**`, 256-expert FP8 MoE

### 🐛 Describe the bug

vLLM correctly identifies that DeepGemm is inaccurate for this model type and logs so at startup:

```
WARNING [vllm.py:1008] Auto-disabled DeepGemm for model_type=qwen3_5_moe_text on Blackwell.
  DeepGemm E8M0 scale format causes accuracy degradation for this architecture.
  Falling back to CUTLASS. To disable DeepGemm globally, set VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0.
```

…and then **selects DeepGemm anyway for the MoE layers**:

```
INFO [fp8.py:405] Using DEEPGEMM Fp8 MoE backend out of potential backends:
  ['AITER', 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'DEEPGEMM', 'TRITON', 'MARLIN', ...]
```

The auto-disable sets `quant_config.use_deep_gemm = False` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), and
`qwen3_5_moe_text` **is** present in `_DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL_EXCLUDED_MODEL_TYPES`
(`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) — so the denylist is doing its job. But `use_deep_gemm` appears to have
**no references anywhere under `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/`**; the FP8 MoE backend
selector honors only the `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM` / `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM` env vars. Net effect: the
denylist covers dense linear layers only, and the MoE layers — where the accuracy concern for an MoE
model actually matters most — still run DeepGemm.

So the warning is truthful about dense layers and silently wrong about MoE.

### Why this surfaced now

**PR #43477** ("Enable DeepSeek V4 and GLM-5.1 on SM120", shipped v0.24.0) added
`is_device_capability_family(120)` to `deep_gemm.py`. Prior to that, the SM100-family gate meant
DeepGemm was never *eligible* on SM121, so this gap was latent. The FP8 MoE backend priority list
itself is unchanged — DeepGemm simply became eligible and started winning

title: [Bugfix] Coerce scalar tool call arguments and reject malformed JSON in _postprocess_messages
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #46328

An assistant message whose `tool_calls[].function.arguments` JSON-decodes to a scalar (e.g. `"\"escaped string\""`, the exact repro payload from the issue) was stored as-is by `_postprocess_messages`, so chat templates that call `arguments.items()` (GLM among others) crash with `'str' object has no attribute 'items'` and the server returns a 500. This PR:
- coerces parsed JSON scalars (`str`/number/bool — and `null`, as before) to `{}`, the same treatment #43862 applied to the `"null"` case, so templates expecting dict arguments don't crash;
- raises `VLLMValidationError` (→ 400 with a clear message) for malformed JSON instead of an unhandled 500.

Dict and list arguments are preserved unchanged.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked before starting and again before opening this PR: the issue timeline has zero cross-referenced PRs, and `gh pr list --search "46328 in:body" --state all` returns empty. The related merged PR #43862 only handled `arguments="null"`; this covers the remaining non-dict cases plus malformed JSON.

New unit tests in `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py`: parametrized scalar cases (`'"escaped string"'`, `"42"`, `"true"`) assert coercion to `{}`, and a malformed-JSON case asserts `VLLMValidationError`. bodyExcerpt:
# Fix Video Temporal Padding Token Estimates

## Summary

Fix incorrect video token estimation when `temporal_patch_size > 2`.
Fix #47866
## Root Cause

Several multimodal models used:

```python
padded_num_frames = num_frames + num_frames % temporal_patch_size
```

This only works reliably for `temporal_patch_size` 1 or 2. For example:

```text
num_frames = 17
temporal_patch_size = 4

current:  17 + 17 % 4 = 18
expected: 20
```

The incorrect padding can make `grid_t` and the estimated video token count too
small. This affects vLLM-side budget estimation, dummy input sizing, and
warmup.

## Changes

title: Preserve DeepSeek sigmoid grouped routing metadata
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

GLM-style DeepSeekV4/DSA models can use sigmoid routing with an expert-score correction bias, norm_topk_prob=True, n_group/topk_group metadata, and a non-unit routed scaling factor. title: Account scheduled spec slots on empty output rows
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The async scheduler reserves output slots before a speculative decode step finishes. For MTP with five draft tokens, a decode step can reserve six output slots: one sampled token slot plus five draft slots. Normal rejection sampling later drains the unmaterialized draft slots after the worker output is applied.

The old accounting only ran when both `scheduled_spec_token_ids` and `generated_token_ids` were non-empty. If the worker row parsed to an empty token list, neither accepted-token application nor rejected-token accounting ran. Repeated empty rows then leaked `num_computed_tokens` and async `num_output_placeholders` until the request reached its model-length scheduling budget with no real output progress.

GLM-5.2 reproduced this with real high-KV MTP traffic. One observed empty-row source was a recovered sampled token equal to `vocab_size`; vLLM 0.24 already contains the upstream sampler boundary fix for that case. This patch keeps the scheduler invariant robust regardless of the empty-row source: if a request had speculative output slots scheduled, every unmaterialized scheduled slot is refunded even when the parsed output row is empty.

The subtle point is the sampled/base slot. Prior upstream discussion in vllm-project/vllm#42722 noted that rolling back only rejected draft tokens is not sufficient for an empty autoregressive row. When no token materializes, the sampled slot must also be rolled back so the request can schedule the same position again instead of remaining one token ahead of concrete output.

For normal rows this reduces to the existing behavior:

- one sampled token and no accepted drafts materialized -> drain all drafts;
- sampled token plus accepted drafts materialized -> drain only the missing scheduled slots;
- all scheduled slots materialized -> drain nothing.

title: [ROCm] Route sparse-indexer decode top-k through AITER dispatcher
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5 sparse attention indexer calls decode top-k on every
decode step. On the ROCm path that call is hardwired to
`torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode` — a HIP radix kernel whose cost grows
~linearly with context width (~15× slower than NVIDIA B200's context-independent
`persistent_topk_kernel`; ~78 calls/step make it the dominant single-kernel gap
at long context).

This routes the call through `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` instead, which gates a
**context-length-independent FlyDSL kernel** onto the arch/shape window where it
wins and keeps HIP everywhere else. vLLM adds **no gfx950 logic** — all
arch/shape routing and the HIP fallback live in AITER.

- Depends on the AITER decode-top-k dispatcher (ROCm/aiter, follow-up to
  https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4355). Until an aiter exposing
  `top_k_per_row_decode` is installed, this path is a **no-op** and the native
  kernel runs unchanged.
- Ticket: SILOTIGER-699 (epic SILOTIGER-606, GLM-5 MI355X perf uplift).

**What changes** — one file, `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`:

1. `_aiter_top_k_per_row_decode()` — cached resolver returning
   `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode` when importable, else `None`.
2. The decode call site calls the resolved op when present, else falls back to
   the existing `torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode`.

Signatures are positionally identical, so the call is drop-in. Behavior when
aiter is absent or predates the dispatcher: resolver returns `None` → native
`_C` kernel, i.e. a no-op on current deployments.

title: [ROCm] Don't re-quantize bf16 MLA kv_b_proj to fp4/fp8 for GLM MoE DSA
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

On ROCm, the AITER MLA path assumes a bf16 `kv_b_proj` is unquantized and
quantizes it to fp4/fp8. This is wrong for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (e.g.
`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`), where the MLA weights are intentionally bf16 and only the
MoE experts are MXFP4.

Quantizing these MLA weights to fp4 adds ~11% error per attention layer. It
accumulates across layers and pushes greedy decoding into repetition loops.

This PR skips fp4/fp8 MLA quantization for GLM MoE DSA (matching SGLang). The MoE
experts stay MXFP4, so the model remains int4.

## Test Plan

Serve `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` on gfx950 with the AITER sparse MLA backend, greedy
(`temperature=0`), `reasoning_effort="high"`:

  "model": "amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France?"}],
  "max_tokens": 200, "temperature": 0.0, "reasoning_effort": "high"
}'
```

Before — repeats indefinitely:

### Summary

This change updates the GLM-4.1V vision model to pass the vision attention head count to `is_vit_use_data_parallel()`, allowing the existing automatic fallback logic to detect when the vision attention heads cannot be evenly partitioned across the configured tensor parallel size.

### Background

The vision helper `is_vit_use_data_parallel(num_heads)` already supports automatically falling back to data parallelism when the number of vision attention heads is not divisible by the tensor parallel size.

However, GLM-4.1V was invoking this helper without providing the vision head count, preventing the fallback logic from being applied during vision module initialization.

* `Glm4vVisionTransformer`

### Motivation

With this change, models whose vision attention head count is not divisible by the tensor parallel size can correctly use the existing vision data-parallel fallback instead of attempting an unsupported tensor-parallel partition.

title: [Bug]: GLM 5.2 MTP didn't work in AMD MI300x
bodyExcerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

GLM-5.2-FP8 with MTP speculative decoding hangs on 8x MI300X (gfx942). Startup finishes, but the engine deadlocks in the vocab-parallel logits all-gather on the first real spec-decode step (RCCL `no transport for peer on channel N`).

**Repro:** `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, ROCm+AITER, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":K}'`.

**Root cause 1 (hits the config above):** warmup runs `compute_logits`' all-gather at 1 row/req, but spec decode verifies `1 + num_speculative_tokens` rows/req. That larger message maps onto extra RCCL channels whose transports connect lazily on first use, and that first use is a live decode step, so the connect fails and hangs.
Fix: after the profile `_dummy_run`, warm `compute_logits` once at `min(max_num_reqs*(1+num_spec_tokens), max_num_tokens)` rows (guarded by `num_spec_tokens > 0`).

**Root cause 2 (only with `--enable-expert-parallel`, TP>1):** under sequence-parallel MoE, MTP's `mtp_block` reduce-scatters its output but `DeepSeekMultiTokenPredictorLayer.forward` never restores full tokens (unlike `DeepseekV2Model.forward`), so ranks feed mismatched token counts into the collective. Same class as the Qwen MTP fix #48429.
Fix: when `hidden_states.shape[0] != positions.shape[0]`, all-gather `[hidden_states, residual]`, slice to full length, and split.

Fix 1 validated e2e on MI300X (coherent output, num_spec=1 accept 75-82%).

title: transformers backend: tensor reshape error during profile run with GLM MoE architecture
bodyExcerpt:
## Description

After fixing the FP8 dispatch issue (separate issue filed), the transformers backend loads the model successfully but crashes during the profile/warmup dummy forward pass with:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'shape '[-1, 8, 576]' is invalid for input of size 16777216'
```

The model loads (103 seconds, all 141 shards) but the profile run fails on a tensor reshape in the MoE expert routing code.

## Root Cause

The transformers backend's model forward path produces incompatible tensor shapes for GLM's grouped MoE architecture during the dummy forward pass. The reshape `[-1, 8, 576]` doesn't match the input size (16777216 = 2048×8192), suggesting the MoE expert routing code in the transformers model implementation is producing incompatible tensor shapes.

This occurs with `--enforce-eager` (no CUDA graphs) and `--max-model-len 4096`.

## Reproduction

```bash
vllm serve <GLM FP8 MoE model> --model-impl transformers --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --enforce-eager --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096
```

Tested with GLM-5.2-FP8 (78-layer MoE, 754B params, GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM architecture) on 8×B200.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.25.1 (built from source with FP8 dispatch fix applied)
- torch: 2.11.0+cu130
- transformers: 5.13.1
- Model: GLM-5.2-FP8 (finegrained FP8 MoE, architecture: GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM)

## Impact

Blocks `--model-impl transformers` for GLM MoE models even after the FP8 dispatch fix. The transformers backend is needed for mid-layer hooks (abliteration, DMEAN, activation steering).

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM DSA with --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla crashes at engine init: KV-cache reshape sizes view by head_size (576) while pages are 656B/token
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

On current main / nightly (`0.25.1.dev37+g3d99b0499`, also reproduced on `1ef1c7ebb`), any DSA-family model (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2 / `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` fails during engine core initialization:

```
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 7259, in _reshape_kv_cache_tensors
    kv_caches[layer_name] = _reshape_attention_kv_cache(
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 251, in _reshape_attention_kv_cache
    kv_cache = kv_raw_tensor.view(dtype).view(permuted_kv_cache_shape)
RuntimeError: shape '[512, 64, 576]' is invalid for input of size 21495808
```

21495808 / (512·64) = 656 — the raw tensor is correctly allocated with the fp8_ds_mla 656-byte-per-token layout, but the target view shape was computed from `head_size` = 576.

### Root cause

`MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` constructs `MLAAttentionSpec` without `kv_quant_mode`, so it stays at the `KVQuantMode.NONE` default. The same pattern exists in both model runners (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`).

The DeepseekV4-specific spec constructor was already fixed this way in #47716 (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py` passes `kv_quant_mode=get_kv_quant_mode(self.kv_cache_dtype)`), which is why DSv4 works while the generic MLA path (V3.2 / GLM DSA) crashes. title: [Bugfix] GLM 5.2: Fix skip_topk on the fused DSA path (MTP index share)
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose
Bug in new optional GLM model definiton.

Fix a crash (and, latently, wrong semantics) in the fused DSA path
(`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/attention.py`) when
`index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is active.

With index share, the proposer toggles `skip_topk=True` for MTP draft steps 1+
(#44420, #45895). `forward()` then correctly passes `index_k=None` /
`index_weights=None`, but `_fused_attention` derived `has_indexer` from
`self.indexer is not None` alone — which is always true on MTP layers — so:

- `fused_norm_rope` immediately fails its `assert index_k is not None`
  (kernels.py:412), crashing the first multi-step proposal; and
- even absent the assert, the unconditional `sparse_attn_indexer` call would
  clear and recompute the shared top-k buffer every draft step, defeating
  index share.

The fix keys `has_indexer` on `index_k is not None` (and gates the `index_q`
GEMM and `sparse_attn_indexer` call on it), routing draft steps into the
kernels' existing `HAS_INDEXER=False` "shared layer" branch: no indexer K/Q
processing, no top-k recompute, and no buffer clear — the sparse attention
reuses the compacted step-0 indices. This matches the reference path, which
skips the indexer under the same flag (`mla.py`:
`if self.indexer and self.is_sparse and not self.skip_topk`).

Reachability: the fused path is opt-in via `model_class_overrides`, and
`index_share_for_mtp_iteration` is currently set only by GLM-5.2 configs
(DeepSeek-V3.2 does not set it)

---

AI assistance was used for this change (analysis, patch, and tests); the
change has been human-reviewed line by line.

title: [Kernel] Extend CuTe DSL skinny GEMM to GLM-5.2
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

### CuTe DSL skinny GEMM

- Add an optional compile-time `K` specialization to the existing CuTe DSL
  skinny GEMM.
- On the static-`K` path, use a compile-time K-tile loop and prefetch the first
  two B tiles before the PDL wait.
- Convert each loaded A/B register tile to FP32 once before FP32 accumulation.
- Keep the existing dynamic-`K` path used by Kimi-K3 unchanged.

### GLM-5.2 mapping

- Extend the existing GLM-5.2 decode selection to use CuTe DSL for the skinny
  cases while retaining DSV3 and the original linear fallback:
  - `qkv_a` and `q_b`: CuTe DSL for M=1-2, DSV3 for M=3-16, original linear
    otherwise.
  - MTP `eh`: CuTe DSL for M=1-3, original `nn.Linear` otherwise.
- Add the GLM-5.2 DSV3 specializations for `qkv_a` and `q_b`.
- Enable the mapping only for `glm_moe_dsa`, unquantized BF16, and exact SM103.
- Preserve the original projection modules, weights, and state-dict layout.

This does not duplicate another open PR. It builds on the Kimi-K3 CuTe DSL
infrastructure added to `main` by #50089 and extends it to GLM-5.2.

8xB300 single node, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP8, fp8 KV cache, MTP=5, model runner v2,

title: [ROCm] [BugFix] Fix Quark GLM-5.2 Checkpoint inference: indexer wk per-channel FP8 dequant + missing sparse-MLA metadata fields
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

This PR addresses two independent bugs blocking quark quantized GLM-5.2 checkpoints with Attn quantized to PTPC FP8 from running end-to-end on ROCm (MI355X / gfx950). 

### Per-channel FP8 scale for fused indexer `wk` (`deepseek_v2.py`):

`_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` dequantizes the FP8 indexer `wk` weight to BF16 at load time so it can be fused with `weights_proj`. However, it unconditionally reads `scale_inv.shape[1]`, assuming a 2-D block-wise scale. Checkpoints that store `wk` with a 1-D per-output-channel scale crash at load with:
```
IndexError: tuple index out of range
# deepseek_v2.py: block_size = weight_fp8.shape[1] // scale_inv.shape[1]
```

Fix Added: branch on `scale_inv.ndim`. For a 1-D scale, use `GroupShape(1, in_features)` (per-output-channel); the original 2-D block path is unchanged. 

### Missing sparse-MLA metadata fields on the ROCm aiter backend:

#47327 refactored the shared MLA forward (`mla_attention.py`) to read `num_decodes`, `num_prefills`, `num_decode_tokens`, and `prefill_max_seq_len` from attention metadata, and updated the FlashMLA / FlashAttn sparse backends accordingly. `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata` was not updated, so inference crashes during graph capture with

```
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata' object has no attribute 'num_decodes'
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata' object has no attribute 'prefill_max_seq_len'
```

The ROCm sparse impl only implements `forward_mqa` (no `forward_mha`), so the dense-MHA prefill path added by #47327 was not viable on ROCm.

title: KVBlockZeroer crashes with non-uniform page sizes on GLM-5.2 FP8
bodyExcerpt:
`KVBlockZeroer` asserts uniform page sizes but GLM-5.2 produces page sizes 2112 vs 10496.

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 660, in initialize_from_config
    self.model_runner._init_kv_zero_meta()
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 522, in _init_kv_zero_meta
    self.kv_block_zeroer = KVBlockZeroer(
File "vllm/v1/worker/utils.py", line 155, in __init__
    assert page_size_el == cur_page_el, (
AssertionError: Non-uniform page sizes: 2112 vs 10496
```

- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`
- Model Runner: V2
- GPU: NVIDIA H200
- Flags: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 1`
- Broken commit: `dd72658e7`
- Last working commit: `94c0ef300180f8fd1071d9cbe7270a8348155f94`

GLM-5.2 uses MLA (`kv_lora_rank: 512`, `v_head_dim: 256`) plus a DSA indexer (`index_n_heads: 32`, `index_head_dim: 128`), producing two KV cache groups with different page sizes.

Root cause is #47574 (`8ce53a616`) which changed `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` from `return self.has_mamba_layers` to `return self.has_mamba_layers or self.has_mixed_precision_kv_cache`. GLM-5.2 with fp8 KV cache has multiple cache groups with different precisions, so zeroing is now enabled, but `KVBlockZeroer` does not handle non-uniform page sizes.

unlike the MXFP4 checkpoints handled by #46757, do NOT list those layers under

crashes while loading the bf16 weights.

(`num_hidden_layers .. num_hidden_layers + num_nextn_predict_layers`) and routes
their MoE experts and linear projections through the unquantized methods,
without editing the checkpoint.

Note: this is orthogonal to #48886 (indexer `wk` per-channel FP8 dequant +
sparse-MLA metadata). The MTP-exclude logic in `quark.py` is not platform- or
scheme-specific, but so far it has only been validated on ROCm (AMD MI350,
gfx950 / MI35x family) with NVFP4 + MTP.

## Test Plan / Result
Served GLM-5.1-NVFP4 with MTP and ran GSM8K 5-shot via lm_eval
(local-completions endpoint). Tested on AMD MI350, TP=8; the fix targets the
gfx950 / MI35x family.

| --- | --- |
| flexible-extract | 0.9507 |
| strict-match | 0.9515 |

title: [ROCm][MLA] Enable AITER sparse MLA decode + MQA-only prefill for GLM DSA
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enables the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend (`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) used by
GLM DSA (Deepseek Sparse Attention) models to run end-to-end.

Two issues were blocking it:

1. **Missing decode/prefill metadata.** The generic `MLAAttention` /
   `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` path expects the attention metadata to expose
   the decode/prefill split counters and prefill metadata (`num_decodes`,
   `num_prefills`, `num_decode_tokens`, `prefill_max_seq_len`, `prefill`). The
   ROCm aiter sparse metadata class did not define these, raising
   `AttributeError` at runtime. Other sparse MLA metadata classes (e.g.
   `FlashMLASparseMetadata`) already expose them.

2. **No dense-MHA prefill.** The ROCm aiter sparse impl only implements the
   top-k MQA path (`forward_mqa`), which handles **both** prefill and decode; it
   has no dense-MHA prefill (`forward_mha`). The generic path still tried to
   build a dense prefill backend and eventually hit `NotImplementedError`.

> Note: this change is code-independent from the Quark MTP-unquantized fix
> (#49187), but that fix is required at runtime to *load* the
> `GLM-5.x-NVFP4` checkpoints used to validate this PR.

## Changes

- `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`
  - Add `num_decodes`, `num_prefills`, `num_decode_tokens`,
    `prefill_max_seq_len`, and `prefill` to `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadata`.
  - Compute them in the metadata builder via `split_decodes_and_prefills`.
  - Add `supports_mha_prefill = False` to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` to advertise
    that it has no dense-MHA prefill path.
- `mla_attention.py`
  - In `MLAAttention.__init__`, when the impl is sparse and does not support
    dense-MHA prefill (`supports_mha_prefill == False`), set
    `prefill_backend = None` so prefill flows through the top-k MQA path instead
    of an unimplemented `forward_mha`.

## Test Plan

- Serve `amd/GLM-5.1-NVFP4` and `amd/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (GLM DSA) on AMD Instinct
  MI350 (gfx950), TP=8, with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.
- Run gsm8k (5-shot, lm_ev

title: [Bugfix] GLM-4.7/4.5 parser: deserialize tool args with no schema type
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The engine rewrite of the GLM parser (#45915) dropped the legacy parser's `_deserialize` step (`json.loads`, then a Python-literal fallback). Type correction is now entirely schema-gated (`_fix_arg_types`), so values with no schema type — keys absent from the tool's `properties`, tools without `properties`, or requests with no tools — come back as JSON strings: `<arg_value>5</arg_value>` → `"5"` (was `5`), `true` → `"true"`, `[1, 2.5]` → `"[1, 2.5]"`. Affects both `glm45` and `glm47` registrations. Same regression class as gemma4's #47906 (being fixed in its own converter in #47909); the GLM parser is not covered by any open PR.

This adds an opt-in `ParserEngineConfig.deserialize_untyped_args` that applies the legacy heuristic to string values without a schema entry, enabled for `glm47_moe`. Schema-declared types still win. Without a schema, streamed trailing values are withheld until complete, since heuristic conversion may change their serialized form and break the streamed-prefix invariant.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm4_moe_tool_parser.py
pytest tests/parser/engine/
```

## Test Result

```
25 passed (glm47 + glm4_moe, incl. 6 new regression tests)
3697 passed (tests/parser/engine)
```

New tests cover: no-schema values typed, undeclared keys typed alongside schema coercion, schema `string` beating the heuristic (`"02139"` stays a string), and streaming == non-streaming at chunk sizes 1 / 7 / whole-output.

No open PR or issue covers this (searched glm47/glm tool parser/deserialize; #47909 is gemma4-only, #48131 was a release-branch backport of a different zero-arg bug). Written with AI assistance; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: LMCache + vLLM: pipeline parallelism now works with MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.6)
bodyExcerpt:
## LMCache + vLLM: pipeline parallelism now works with MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.6)

Just wanted to give a heads-up here because I've seen a few issues pop up about LMCache + PP not working, and I've put up a fix on the LMCache side that unblocks it.

### What was broken

If you tried to run vLLM with LMCache in multi-server MP mode with `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`, the connector would refuse to start with:

```
ValueError: LMCacheMPConnector multi-server mode only supports
tensor parallelism (TP), not pipeline parallelism (PP). Got pp_size=2.
```

This hit especially hard for MLA models (Kimi K2, GLM-4.5/4.6) because those are exactly the workloads where you want both PP (to fit a large model across nodes) and LMCache (to cut TTFT on long-context agentic workloads).

### Why it was blocked

The guard existed because of a subtle read-lock refcounting bug. `compute_extra_count` in LMCache inferred whether a model used MLA by checking `tp > world_size`. That heuristic is correct when PP=1 but breaks under PP>1 — PP inflates `world_size` to `tp × pp`, so the inference produces `extra_count = 0` when it should be `tp_size - 1`. Result: the server under-locks, multiple workers race on the same KV chunk, and you get premature eviction.

### The fix

I opened [LMCache PR #4082](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4082) that:

1. Carries an explicit `use_mla` flag in the cache key (instead of inferring it) — backward-compatible on the wire
2. Fixes `kv_tp_size` and `is_kv_writer` in `ParallelStrategy` to account for the fact that server blocks align with PP stages, not TP groups
3. Propagates `use_mla` across all client adapters (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, SDK)

No vLLM-side changes are needed — vLLM's in-tree connector already imports from the `lmcache` package, so once the LMCache fix lands and users update, it picks up the fix automatically. I verified that `model_config.use_mla` is correctly set for both `kimi_linear` and `glm4_moe_lite` in vLLM's `is_deepseek_

## Results (20 identical requests)

| temp | Pass rate | Failure |

| `>0` (sampling) | **18/20 (90%)** | `finish_reason=stop` + malformed content |
| `=0` (greedy) | **20/20 (100%)** ✅ | None |

title: [Bugfix] Recycle post-final-norm hidden in GLM MTP (single norm)
bodyExcerpt:
The compile-free DeepseekV32 MTP draft layer returned the pre-final-norm hidden as both the draft-logits hidden and the recycled previous_hidden_states. Recycling the pre-final-norm hidden mismatches the draft model's hnorm and drops MTP acceptance; the reference deepseek_mtp.py (PR #45895) recycles the post-final-norm hidden.

Fix by computing the post-final-norm hidden once -- fusing the residual-add into the final RMSNorm (fused_add_rms_norm) -- and returning it for both tuple positions. compute_logits then applies the LM head only (no second RMSNorm), so the norm count is unchanged (one per draft step per layer) while the recycled hidden is now correctly post-norm.

The tuple return is understood by both the V2 speculator (isinstance-tuple check in autoregressive/speculator.py) and the legacy proposer (model_returns_tuple() is True for the DeepSeekMTPModel architecture used by GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2). SharedHead and the proposer contracts are unchanged.
